data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 argues that a decentralized network is 'strictly less resilient' than a centralized service when algorithmic convergence synchronizes the network. But this directly contradicts the problem's framing that the centralized service has 'strictly more total internal redundancy.' Even if the decentralized network synchronizes and forfeits its independence advantage, a synchronized N-node network failing together still has N independent physical instances failing simultaneously, whereas the centralized service's strictly greater internal redundancy means it has even more total redundant components. SRC_001 never explains how losing the independence advantage results in being strictly LESS resilient than a service with strictly more total redundancy. A synchronized decentralized network and a centralized service with greater internal redundancy could fail at the same time, but the centralized one has more redundant components to potentially isolate or absorb the failure. Thus, 'strictly less resilient' overstates the case.
